metadata.title: Voice Khata Edge Case and Reliability Dataset
metadata.description: Synthetic scenarios for evaluating a multilingual voice-based kirana customer credit/payment ledger. Includes speech, language, amount, customer, transaction, correction, date, context, database, network, AI, security, UX, performance and reminder cases.
metadata.provenance: The hackathon constraints are derived from the user's provided Gnani Voice Hackathon problem statement. The detailed edge cases and training examples are synthetic engineering recommendations created for this project.
metadata.important_usage_note: This file is a starter dataset for intent/slot extraction and application testing. It is not sufficient by itself to train an STT acoustic model. STT training requires consented audio paired with accurate transcripts. For an LLM, use the labelled examples as seed examples, expand them with human-reviewed utterances, and keep evaluation data separate from training data.
metadata.privacy_note: All names, amounts and examples are synthetic. Do not add real shop/customer financial records without appropriate consent, protection and retention controls.

priority_definitions.P0: Critical financial, privacy or data-integrity failure; block release if failing.
priority_definitions.P1: High-priority voice/AI reliability or hackathon behaviour; fix before live demo.
priority_definitions.P2: Usability/performance robustness; implement where time allows.

metadata.format_note: UTF-8 JSON. Amounts are represented in integer paise in labelled examples where applicable. Human-readable expected behaviour is not executable code.

hackathon_constraints.requirement: Use Gnani Prisma v3.0 for STT
Use Gnani Timbre v3.0 for TTS
WebSocket streaming only; no telephony or phone numbers
Orchestration may be Pipecat, LiveKit or custom; hosted end-to-end agent platforms cannot be the core loop
Recognise amounts under shop noise, including spoken number variants
Parse customer, amount, credit/payment and relative dates
Ask a short question when two customers share a name
Answer spoken ledger questions within two seconds of the question ending
hackathon_constraints.basis: PS2 required feature / target to measure

hackathon_constraints.requirement: Reminders are polite and only sent to customers who opted in
Ledger data stays on-device or is encrypted at rest
AI disclosure in the first turn
Synthetic or consented data only; protect and delete demo transcripts after judging
Keep API keys out of public repositories

core_invariants.description: If the amount is missing, ambiguous, malformed or uncertain, ask a clarification; do not commit.
Resolve customer through the authenticated shop's directory; ask when zero or multiple candidates exist.
Credit, payment, refund, adjustment and future promise are distinct operations.
Read back customer, amount, type and date as configured; commit only after required confirmation.

core_invariants.rule: LLM is not source of truth
core_invariants.description: LLM extracts intent/slots; backend validates and database determines transaction status and balance.
One logical transaction request may be committed at most once, even if events or requests are retried.
Do not silently overwrite committed financial history; use linked reversal/replacement or adjustment records.
Use integer paise or fixed-precision decimal arithmetic, never binary floating point for stored financial amounts.
Every read/write is scoped to the authenticated shop and authorised user.
Only confirm success after the backend verifies the database commit.
A promised future payment must never be recorded as money already received.
Use intentional user interaction and confirmation; do not treat arbitrary background speech as authorised intent.
Send reminders only to customers who opted in for that channel; respect revocation.
Minimise, protect, restrict and delete transcripts/audio according to the applicable policy and hackathon requirements.
Retries must be limited, idempotent and observable; do not retry financial writes blindly.

intent.description: Must be one of the supported intent names.

entities.description: Extracted slots. Missing/uncertain fields must remain absent or null, never be guessed.

recommended_evaluation_metrics.name: intent_accuracy
recommended_evaluation_metrics.definition: Correct intent predictions divided by evaluated utterances.

recommended_evaluation_metrics.name: slot_exact_match
recommended_evaluation_metrics.definition: Exact match for customer, amount, transaction type and date fields where present.

recommended_evaluation_metrics.name: amount_exact_match
recommended_evaluation_metrics.definition: Percentage of monetary amounts extracted exactly correctly.

recommended_evaluation_metrics.name: customer_resolution_accuracy
recommended_evaluation_metrics.definition: Correct unique customer selected; ambiguous cases must result in clarification.

recommended_evaluation_metrics.name: unsafe_commit_rate
recommended_evaluation_metrics.definition: Transactions committed despite missing, invalid or ambiguous required information; target zero.

recommended_evaluation_metrics.name: duplicate_commit_rate
recommended_evaluation_metrics.definition: Duplicate logical transactions committed; target zero.

recommended_evaluation_metrics.name: ledger_reconciliation_accuracy
recommended_evaluation_metrics.definition: Calculated balances agree with the authoritative transaction ledger.

recommended_evaluation_metrics.name: time_to_first_audio
recommended_evaluation_metrics.definition: Time from end of user speech to first assistant audio; measure against hackathon target.

recommended_evaluation_metrics.name: clarification_precision
recommended_evaluation_metrics.definition: Clarification is requested when needed, and unnecessary clarification is minimised.

recommended_evaluation_metrics.name: recovery_success_rate
recommended_evaluation_metrics.definition: Percentage of simulated transient failures safely recovered without lost or duplicated writes.
